Title: ECMA 335 II.15.2 Static, instance, and virtual methods
Description: Hello all

We have two notices in this article

-  Instance methods on classes (including boxed value types), have a this pointer that is
by default an object reference to the class on which the method is defined.

-  Instance methods on (unboxed) value types, have a this pointer that is by default a
managed pointer to an instance of the type on which the method is defined.

What is a difference between a **object reference** and **managed pointer** in this case?
